decisions.reason: The net price display plugin is cheap to maintain and close to the core shop offer, so management will likely attribute its lower website visibility to portfolio presentation rather than failure and keep it.
The ERP interface represents the largest sunk development investment and is central to the announced multichannel direction, so management is strongly inclined to persist with it.
As the lead price comparison tracking plugin it fits the measurable-marketing positioning, and the firm will likely keep it as the version into which overlapping variants are consolidated.
It duplicates the other tracking plugins and was absent from the website in 2020–2021, so consolidating the overlapping variants is the easiest way to free resources despite the sunk cost.
As a third overlapping price comparison plugin with no recent visibility, it carries little public commitment, which makes it a natural candidate for consolidation.
The net price reporting plugin complements Product A and the analytics focus, so management can still justify keeping it despite its lack of recent visibility.
